prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
# Summary: A Vision for National Renewal

This manifesto presents a comprehensive plan for national transformation, built on the premise that the country has experienced 14 years of instability, declining public services, and broken promises. The document outlines five core missions designed to address systemic challenges.

## Economic Strategy

The economic approach centres on stability and growth. Strict fiscal rules require balancing day-to-day spending with revenues while ensuring debt falls as a share of the economy. The plan rejects unfunded commitments and prioritises partnership between government and business.

A new industrial strategy will be established with statutory footing, focusing on sectors where the country holds competitive advantages: research institutions, professional services, advanced manufacturing, and creative industries. A National Wealth Fund, capitalised at £7.3 billion, will invest in ports, manufacturing, and clean energy infrastructure, targeting three pounds of private investment for every public pound spent.

Planning reform features prominently, with commitments to build 1.5 million homes, update national planning frameworks, restore mandatory housing targets, and create new towns. Business rates will be reformed to level competition between high streets and online retailers.

## Energy Transformation

The manifesto commits to clean electricity by 2030 through doubling onshore wind, tripling solar power, and quadrupling offshore wind. A publicly-owned energy company will be established, headquartered in Scotland, to partner with industry on clean power deployment.

Existing oil and gas licences will continue, but no new exploration licences will be issued. The windfall tax on energy companies will be extended and increased. A £6.6 billion investment will upgrade five million homes for energy efficiency.

## Public Safety

The approach to crime emphasises neighbourhood policing, with thousands of additional officers funded through efficiency programmes. New powers will address antisocial behaviour, including banning persistent offenders from town centres.

Knife crime reduction targets halving incidents within a decade through mandatory intervention for young people caught carrying weapons, banning certain blade types, and creating youth support hubs. Violence against women will be addressed through specialist police units, fast-tracked court cases, and domestic abuse experts in emergency services.

## Education and Opportunity

Educational reform includes recruiting 6,500 new teachers, establishing free breakfast clubs in all primary schools, and opening 3,000 nurseries in primary school buildings. The curriculum will be reviewed to ensure broader preparation for work and life.

Further education will see the creation of Technical Excellence Colleges and reform of apprenticeship funding into a more flexible skills levy. Higher education funding will be reviewed to create sustainable models.

## Healthcare

The health mission targets returning to 18-week treatment standards through two million additional annual appointments. Investment includes doubling diagnostic scanners, recruiting 8,500 mental health staff, and establishing neighbourhood health centres integrating various services.

Dentistry receives specific attention with 700,000 additional urgent appointments and contract reform. Social care will move toward national standards with a "home first" principle.

## Constitutional Reform

Governance changes include establishing an Ethics and Integrity Commission, modernising parliamentary procedures, and removing hereditary peers from the upper chamber. Voting age will be lowered to 16.

Devolution will be strengthened through new frameworks for collaboration with Scotland, Wales, and Northern Ireland, including a Council of Nations and Regions bringing together national and regional leaders.

## International Relations

Foreign policy emphasises rebuilding alliances while maintaining independence from European political structures. The commitment to the transatlantic alliance and nuclear deterrent remains absolute. A strategic defence review will assess capabilities against current threats.

Relations with European neighbours will be reset through veterinary agreements, professional qualification recognition, and security cooperation, without rejoining single market or customs union arrangements.

Climate leadership will be restored through international partnerships and a Clean Power Alliance. Development spending will return to 0.7% of national income when fiscal conditions permit.
